locator.section: 8 Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Eq. 8.46, inductive branch)

evidence.curator_note: Inductive (i) cleavage of the O-ionized di-n-hexyl ether molecular ion: the charge site O1(+) draws the C7-O1 sigma bonding pair fully onto oxygen, so the C7-O1 bond breaks heterolytically to give the n-hexyl cation C6H13(+) (m/z 85, 77%) and the neutral n-hexyloxy radical .O-C6H13 (the odd electron stays on O1). Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs: the 'i' label sits on a reaction-pathway arrow with the radical loss '-.OC6H13' written beside it; no curved arrow is drawn. Encoded as ONE double-barbed (2-electron) heterolytic arrow: the C7-O1 bonding pair moves onto O1 (becomes an O1 lone pair), leaving C7 as the primary carbocation. The validator's soft note 'lone pair rather than radicals' on atom 1 is expected: the arriving pair is a lone pair, not two radicals.

evidence.curator_note: No MØD rule is cross-linked: rule_index.json has no by_equation entry for 8.46. Detected-ion m/z 85.1006 is the curator-computed monoisotopic value for C6H13+ (electron mass subtracted); printed abundance 77% (relative_intensity 0.77) is a 70 eV EI value. This i-cleavage of the OE(+.) molecular ion is the one-step route to C6H13+; the two-step route (via the m/z-115 oxocarbenium) is IMS8-EQ8.46c and feeds the SAME m/z-85 peak.
